fcc-test-contracts.purpose: Dependency-free shared web-boundary kernel: provider API DTOs, the route/operation/schema contract, the compatibility checker and its export/check scripts, plus the primitives every web surface needs to sit behind HTTP — access policy, auth config and OIDC principal resolution, correlation and trace sampling, metrics, rate-limit policy, health-probe paths, and the extraction lane policy itself. Owns no provider vocabulary and no domain model: it is the layer three lanes can share without inheriting each other's measurement semantics.

PC-global instrument exclusion (per-PC mode exclusivity 2026-08-16, item 3). A chamber PC either accepts web sessions or runs the provider's local program; installation is the primary separation and this is the mistake insurance. It sits in the shared lane on purpose: the exclusion has to bind FCC's GUI, KC's MPTool and mmWave's own program alike, and putting it in a provider entrypoint would make it FCC-only, which is the exact failure the policy exists to prevent. Stdlib only (os/tempfile/pathlib + msvcrt/fcntl). Both entrypoints call it and neither owns the decision: src/session_node_entry.py wraps it in the surface's SessionNodeAlreadyRunning vocabulary (exit 3 contract unchanged, and PC-global subsumes the old port-keyed exclusion), src/main_entry.py acquires inside the startup gate before any window shows. Two refusals stay distinct because the operator action differs (close the other process vs fix the environment) — the superseded _ProcessLock collapsed both into one message. Known limitation, written in the module: tempfile.gettempdir() may resolve per-user, so cross-account exclusivity does not hold; today both processes run as the same tester account (operator ruling), and the machine-global location is a blocking prerequisite for the service migration.

Claimed 2026-08-22 because two lane modules now import it and a box must carry its own import closure, not just its layer: rate_limit_policy derives the credential account budget from LOCKOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS (the "+1" that keeps the database lockout reachable) and credential_throttle uses fingerprint_digest as the anonymisation SSOT. It was owned by no lane until then — no lane module imported it, so the boundary gate had nothing to say.

peer-axis observation verdict (pure, stdlib only) — whether the peer budget is really charged per caller on THIS deployment, as opposed to whether the server is merely configured to restore the real address. Proxy-trust judgement (pure, stdlib only) — which sources may be believed to be our own reverse proxy. It belongs beside rate_limit_policy rather than in the measurement kernel because it decides nothing about measurement: it answers a question every web surface asks and none of the chamber code does — whether the transport source address is the caller's or the gateway's, which is what makes the peer rate-limit tier mean 'per caller' at all.

fcc-test-contracts.entries_note: Re-cut along the surface axis on 2026-08-29 (headless-contract-axis): three kind-of-table modules (api_contract_dtos/operations/schemas) were replaced by six surface modules plus five assembly/shared modules. The entry list moved because LANE MEMBERSHIP moved — this manifest enumerates the lane file by file, so a file-level refactor of the lane makes the declaration stale by construction, and leaving it stale is not "not touching it": the staged tree then cannot import itself (ModuleNotFoundError on the modules the facade now reads) while the cross-lane baseline reports the lane importing nine modules it supposedly does not own. The axis was measured from this surface's own history rather than chosen — the kind-of-table split kept 38% of feature commits inside one file against 86% for this one — and the measurement is re-runnable (scripts/measure_contract_decomposition_axis.py). No depends_on, source_root, forbidden_external or baseline value changed: this is the same lane, enumerated after its files moved.

Re-cut 2026-08-29 (headless-contract-axis): the three kind-of-table modules left and eleven surface/assembly modules arrived. This list and `entries` are the same fact stated twice — ownership and relocation — and test_declared_moves_agree_with_declared_ownership exists because they once disagreed for thirty platform entries. Editing one without the other is the shape that test catches.
fcc-test-contracts.relinquished_paths_note: Box-relative paths whose ownership the monorepo has HANDED OVER to the public repository. They are no longer produced by extraction, and a delivery must not remove them. ⚠️ A declaration is required because observation cannot tell this apart from a file that simply died: both look like 'the previous delivery owned it and this one does not', and the correct action is opposite. Box-relative rather than monorepo-relative because the question this answers is about the receiving tree, and the monorepo path no longer exists to spell.

test_lane_attribution.rule: A test belongs to the lane that owns the source it exercises, and the only machine-readable evidence of that is what it imports. Owners are reduced along depends_on: a test touching both the contracts lane and the platform lane exercises the platform, because the platform is the thing that depends on contracts. Deriving this is the point — 754 hand-maintained rows would be the same shape SPLIT-1 and SPLIT-2 had to repay, where the next file added is the one nobody adds to the list.

retained_reasons.monorepo_test_no_lane_source: The file imports no first-party module: it exercises the repository itself (documentation ownership, CI cost policy, the audit gates) or is shared harness — tests/fakes, fixtures, golden data. It travels with no lane because it tests no lane’s source. Non-Python files under the test root are test data and resolve the same way.
retained_reasons.monorepo_test_crosses_sibling_lanes: The file reaches two lanes that neither depends on the other — in practice the platform and the provider. No single extracted repository will contain both, so the test cannot travel with either and stays in the monorepo.
retained_reasons.monorepo_test_repo_wide_governance: Its imports resolve to exactly one lane, but its assertions audit the whole repository tree (a PROJECT_ROOT-relative glob over tests/ or scripts/), which import-based attribution cannot see — that is a content question, and this manifest's whole design is to answer ownership from imports only. Declared by path in monorepo_governance_tests, each with a mandatory reason, rather than inferred.

Per-pair so a fix in one direction cannot mask a new violation in another. Ratchet down only, and a key that reaches 0 stays listed: deleting it would make a re-introduced edge look like a brand-new pair instead of a regression. Re-measured 2026-08-15 (platform-provider-crossing-closure). fcc-test-platform -> fcc-unlicensed-headless @ src ratchets 9 -> 4 by ownership redeclaration alone — not one line of Python changed, and every candidate was measured before it was written down rather than argued for. Four modules were owned by the directory they sit in rather than the question they answer: central_id_resolver.py (its production sibling postgres_central_id_resolver.py was already platform-owned), session_identity.py (it names CENTRAL rows), outbox_envelope_builder.py (it builds the dict platform_ingestion consumes) move to the platform lane, and report_output_download.py (standard library only, read by the platform download proxy AND the provider headless route) moves to the contracts lane. The distinction is load-bearing and was measured, not assumed: moving any of the first three alone RAISES fcc-unlicensed-headless -> fcc-test-platform @ src from 5 to 6, because outbox_envelope_builder imports the other two — only the closure closes. And moving report_output_download to the platform lane instead would have raised the same reverse pair, because a primitive both lanes read belongs to neither of them. That is the difference between closing a crossing and relocating one, and a per-pair baseline is what makes the difference visible. The same measurement then decided the last two of that pair: problem_response.py and rate_limit_middleware.py carry no provider vocabulary at all and all three web surfaces read them, so platform ownership was measured to RAISE the reverse pair 5 -> 9, and contracts ownership as-written turns 2 cross-lane imports into 3 staged import violations on a lane whose baseline is 0. Both modules were made framework-free instead (the exception class and JSON response constructor are arguments, resolved by the three create_*_app factories inside the guarded try that already raises RuntimeError('FastAPI is required')), and only then claimed. 4 -> 2. forbidden_external is unchanged and staged_import_violation_baseline['fcc-test-contracts'] stays 0. governance.composition_root_crossings_note: Per-site record of what each declared composition root reaches across a lane boundary, and what happens to that site at split time. Added 2026-08-27 because composition_roots was a *file-level* exemption: ExtractionLanePolicy.cross_lane_imports skipped the whole file, so a declared root could accumulate an unbounded, unreasoned set of crossings and no axis would ask. Measured by disabling that one predicate and changing nothing else: the axis reports 50 crossings with the exemption on and 69 with it off, so 19 were invisible — 12 of them in fcc-unlicensed-headless -> fcc-test-platform @ src, the direction a provider/platform split depends on most. Six of the eleven declared roots carry zero crossings, which is why the blanket exemption is slack rather than a property of the category. The staged axis had the opposite blind spot: check_extraction_import_boundaries.py contains the string "composition" zero times, so it does not exempt these files at all and folds them into a single integer, staged_import_violation_baseline. A count cannot see a swap, and this note is where that stopped being hypothetical: src/platform_api_composition.py imported get_logger twice — the lane-neutral application.common.logging_channel at line 36 (e625c694, 2026-08-21) and the provider logger_config at line 144 (cb117ea8, 2026-05-27) — and because Python binds the later import, the contracts-lane one was dead for three months while the count stayed 6. Judged by SET EQUALITY against the production predicate, not by a count, so an added, removed, or swapped site is red and names itself. Dispositions are a closed vocabulary of SEVEN tokens, and the gate executes rather than trusts the ones that make a checkable claim: redundant_today must name a replacement that resolves and that the same file already imports; reowning_blocked_by_residual must actually raise a pair when the target is re-owned, with the declared residual equal to the measured cause; root_to_root must target another declared root. same_lane_after_reowning was in the first draft of this axis and was DELETED when measurement refuted it — re-owning either chamber adapter raises fcc-test-platform -> fcc-unlicensed-headless @ src from 0 to 1 (residuals: application.session.api_contracts and logger_config respectively), so "re-declare ownership, no code change" was false for every candidate. Ownership comes from source_files/source_roots, not entries; a first what-if that edited entries changed nothing while looking like "no impact", which is why the check asserts the mutation applied before reading any result. split_blocker_undecided is mandatory vocabulary, not a placeholder to avoid: assigning a disposition to a site whose fate is an operator decision would be choosing on the operator behalf. Thirteen sites started there; the operator decided the GUI axis on 2026-08-27 and bootstrap.py five moved to decided_repair_pending, leaving eight.
